name: ANITA
summary: A series of long-duration Antarctic balloon flights searched for coherent radio pulses from the highest-energy neutrinos over enormous volumes of polar ice.
detection_principle: A high-altitude array of dual-polarisation horn antennas measured nanosecond radio impulses. Askaryan signals from showers in ice were distinguished from geomagnetic air-shower emission and anthropogenic backgrounds.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The documented four-flight ANITA programme is historical; PUEO is its successor.

collaboration.name: ANITA Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Fourth flight
key_parameters.value: 28 days during December 2016; earlier flights in 2006, 2008 and 2014

results.summary: Each of two blind searches retained one signal-region event compatible with its background estimate; flux limits were reported rather than a neutrino discovery.
Anomalous air-shower-like events motivate follow-up; they do not by themselves establish an astrophysical tau-neutrino flux.
